body.additional_description: Every theme was written on a single hardware synth, then pushed through worn cassette machines until it sounded like a memory of the city rather than the city itself.
body.description: An animated noir feature about a rookie detective and a city that never quite wakes up. Aren built the score from detuned synths and rain-soaked tape loops.

instruments.text: A modular patch run through three cassette decks, each slightly slower than the last, so every note arrives with a little drift and hiss.
instruments.title: Tape synth

body.title: Nightfall Precinct

body.additional_description: Over four hours of adaptive music respond to the player in real time, layering percussion and voices as battles escalate.
body.description: A sprawling fantasy role-playing game where every region has its own musical language, from mountain choirs to desert drums.

instruments.text: Pots, chains and timber beams recorded in an old boat shed, then layered into a rhythm section no orchestra could play.
instruments.title: Found percussion

instruments.text: Wet fingertips on spinning glass bowls give the elven cities their shimmering, slightly unsettling glow.
instruments.title: Glass harmonica

instruments.text: A hand-carved replica flute with a breathy, uneven tone, used for the oldest ruins in the game.
instruments.title: Bone flute

instruments.text: Twelve tubas and contrabass trombones recorded in a stone church for the weight of the dragon themes.
instruments.title: Low brass choir

instruments.text: Tuned down a fifth and played with an e-bow, it carries the lonely travelling theme between towns.
instruments.title: Baritone guitar

body.title: Embers of Aldrath

body.additional_description: Surf rock, spaghetti western, synth horror and lounge jazz all share the same five-note motif, hidden in a different disguise each episode.
body.description: A pulpy road-trip anthology where each episode borrows a different B-movie genre, and the score changes costume every week.

instruments.text: A synth voice designed from recordings of a revving V8, pitched to play the main riff.
instruments.title: Engine synth

instruments.text: A pair of vintage condenser mics placed far from the band to capture the sweaty, roadhouse sound of the room.
instruments.title: Room microphones

instruments.text: Aren wrote and sang the show’s fictional jukebox hit, recorded live in one take.
instruments.title: Lead vocal

songs.title: High Noon at the Gas Pump

body.title: Redline Country

body.additional_description: The score leans on solo voice and bowed piano strings, staying almost silent until the story finally cracks open.
body.description: A slow-burn psychological thriller set in a remote forest lodge, where three friends start to doubt what they remember.

instruments.text: The strings were tracked in a timber-lined hall chosen for its warm, close sound.
instruments.title: Wooden scoring stage

instruments.text: A wordless soprano line becomes the voice of the forest itself.
instruments.title: Solo soprano

instruments.text: The film premiered at an independent festival with a live string quartet performing the opening cue.
instruments.title: Festival premiere

body.title: Hollow Pines

body.additional_description: Big brassy action cues collide with tiny ukulele punchlines, because the jokes land better when the music takes itself too seriously.
body.description: An adult animated comedy about a crew of low-budget superheroes who keep saving the city by accident.

instruments.text: A bright, jangly twelve-string carries the theme song and most of the cheerful disasters.
instruments.title: Twelve-string guitar

body.title: Skyline Misfits

body.additional_description: Each short runs under five minutes, so every cue has to set the scene, land the gag and get out in a handful of bars.
body.description: A collection of animated shorts about tiny glowing creatures who throw dance parties in the dark.

instruments.text: Spring reverb and a vintage tremolo pedal give the bugs their bouncy, retro swagger.
instruments.title: Surf guitar

instruments.text: A felt-dampened grand piano plays the lullaby that closes every short.
instruments.title: Grand piano

body.title: Glowbugs

body.additional_description: The score shifts style as the pilot crosses each region, from frontier western to cosmic choir, mirroring a journey through genres.
body.description: A sci-fi adventure film following a stranded pilot across a desert planet, scored with equal parts orchestra and electronics.

instruments.text: A sixty-piece orchestra recorded over two days, with the brass section split across two rooms.
instruments.title: Scoring session

instruments.text: An acoustic guitar played with a cello bow creates the wind-like texture heard over the dunes.
instruments.title: Bowed guitar

body.title: Dunes of Kharos

body.additional_description: Aren joined part of the shoot at sea, recording hydrophone audio that later became the bed of the score.
body.description: A wildlife docuseries that follows the ocean’s top predators, from kelp forests to the open blue.

instruments.text: Long days on a research boat, recording the ocean between camera dives.
instruments.title: Field crew

instruments.text: Underwater microphones captured whale calls and reef crackle used throughout the score.
instruments.title: Hydrophones

instruments.text: A close encounter that shaped the slow, circling theme of the third episode.
instruments.title: Cage dive

instruments.text: Behind the scenes with the percussion section tracking the finale.

body.title: Apex Waters

body.additional_description: The theme song doubles as the heroes’ garage-band anthem, and returns in a new arrangement every episode.
body.description: An animated superhero series about teenage friends juggling homework, band practice and saving their neighbourhood.

instruments.text: Recording the main theme with a live band and a choir of the voice cast.

instruments.text: A wobbly, comic bass clarinet line for the series’ most dramatic (and least competent) villain.
